info.name: Wikidata Taxonomy Explorer
info.description:
Interactive exploration of Wikidata's knowledge graph for Perspectize content categorization.

Three APIs:
1. SPARQL Endpoint — structured queries for hierarchical data
2. Entity Search (Action API) — find entity IDs by name
3. REST API — get full entity details by ID

No API key required. Rate limits: 5 parallel queries, 60s compute/minute.
Always set User-Agent header (Wikidata blocks default agents).

request.description:
Search for entities by name. Returns entity IDs (Q-numbers), labels, descriptions.

Try changing 'search' to: Presbyterian Church, Taylor Swift, Machine Learning, etc.

Key fields in response:
- id: Q223522 (the Wikidata entity ID)
- label: Kansas City Chiefs
- description: National Football League franchise...

Minimal SPARQL query to confirm endpoint works.

Looks up 3 known entities: Kansas City Chiefs (Q223522), NFL (Q1215884), Presbyterianism (Q178169).

Response shape:
- head.vars: ['item', 'itemLabel', 'itemDescription']
- results.bindings: [ { item: { type: 'uri', value: '...' }, itemLabel: { type: 'literal', value: '...' } } ]

If this returns data, you're good to go.

All American football teams in the NFL.

Key properties used:
- P31 (instance of) = Q17156793 (American football team)
- P118 (league) = Q1215884 (NFL)
- P115 (home venue) — stadium

To get NBA teams: change Q17156793 to Q13393265 (basketball team) and Q1215884 to Q53232 (NBA).
To get MLB: Q476028 (baseball team) + Q132427 (MLB).
To get Premier League: Q476028 (association football club) + Q9448 (PL).

Every Kansas City Chiefs season on record.

Property P5138 = 'sports season of league or competition' linked to the team.

This is the granularity Google NL can't provide — individual seasons for specific teams.

Replace Q223522 with any team Q-number to get their seasons.

Reference query for major US sports leagues.

Q1215884 = NFL, Q53232 = NBA, Q132427 = MLB, Q1147187 = MLS, Q854068 = NHL, Q43325 = Premier League, Q324867 = La Liga.

Use these IDs in other queries to get teams for any league.

Traverse the full class hierarchy for Kansas City Chiefs.

Pattern: P31 (instance of) then P279* (zero or more subclass of).

This shows: American football team → sports team → organization → group of humans → entity.

This is the Wikidata equivalent of a taxonomy path. Replace Q223522 with any entity.

Search for denominations by name.

Try: Presbyterian, Baptist, Methodist, Lutheran, Pentecostal, Orthodox, Catholic, Reformed, Anglican.

Note the Q-numbers returned — use them in SPARQL queries to explore further.

Reference lookup of major Christian denomination families with their Q-numbers.

Use these Q-numbers to drill deeper — e.g., find all specific Presbyterian denominations.

Find organizations with religion (P140) = Presbyterianism.

Shows specific Presbyterian bodies like Presbyterian Church (USA), Presbyterian Church in America, etc.

Change Q178169 to Q93191 (Baptist), Q33203 (Methodist), etc. for other families.

Reference lookup of world religions with Q-numbers.

Use these as starting points for exploring branches, denominations, and traditions within each religion.

Music genres with parent genre relationships.

P31 (instance of) Q188451 (music genre), P279 (subclass of) for hierarchy.

Shows: hip hop → popular music, jazz → music, etc.

All video game genres in Wikidata.

Q659563 = video game genre.

Shows: first-person shooter, battle royale, RPG, MOBA, etc.

All film genres in Wikidata.

Q201658 = film genre.

Shows: action, comedy, documentary, thriller, horror, etc.

Academic disciplines and fields of science.

Q11862829 = academic discipline.

Shows: physics, biology, computer science, etc. with parent fields.

Programming languages with programming paradigm.

Q9143 = programming language, P3966 = programming paradigm.

Shows: Go, Python, Rust, etc. with functional/OOP/etc. paradigm.

Walk UP the class hierarchy from any entity to root.

Pattern: entity → P31 (instance of) → P279* (subclass of, recursive)

Replace Q223522 (Chiefs) with any entity ID.

This is the Wikidata equivalent of building a taxonomy breadcrumb path.

Walk DOWN from a class to find all instances.

Pattern: ?item → P31/P279* (instance of / subclass chain) → target class

This finds all NFL teams by looking for anything that's an instance of 'American football team' (Q17156793) in league NFL (Q1215884).

Replace the target class to explore any category.

Get direct subclasses of a class (one level down only).

Q349 = sport. Shows: team sport, water sport, combat sport, etc.

Pattern: ?subclass P279 (subclass of) → target. No * = direct only.

Great for building taxonomy trees level by level.

See ALL properties and values for any entity.

Replace Q223522 with any entity ID.

Shows: instance of, league, home venue, country, sport, head coach, etc.

Useful for discovering which properties are available for a type of entity.

Properties of YouTube itself (Q866) in Wikidata.

See what Wikidata knows about YouTube — owner, launch date, programming language, etc.

YouTube channels tracked in Wikidata, sorted by subscriber count.

Q36834616 = YouTube channel, P8814 = number of subscribers.

Not comprehensive but shows that Wikidata tracks YouTube-specific entities.
